unresolved: n_models=3 counts Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and SVM as classifiers this paper itself trains/evaluates (Table 2); Random Forest is the headline model used throughout the rest of the paper.

n_baselines=3 counts Naive Bayes, SVM, and PJScan as comparison points against the Random Forest result; there is overlap with n_models since NB/SVM are both internally-evaluated alternatives and comparison baselines -- the paper does not clearly separate these roles.

n_seeds=5 ('5 independent trials using 10-fold cross validation') is stated only for the mimicry-effectiveness (Table 10) and perturbation (Table 12) adversarial-analysis experiments; the primary ben/mal and opp/tar classification results (Tables 3-6, Figures 3-6) use 10-fold cross-validation but do not state a repeated-trial count.

control_arm='clean' is a best-fit mapping: this is a malware-classification paper (benign vs malicious PDFs), not a backdoor-attack-on-ML-models paper, so the benign document set serves as the natural clean reference class rather than a clean-vs-poisoned-model control.
reports_variability='figure' reflects the explicit 95% CI in Figure 2; Tables 2, 10, and 12 report only averages across repeated runs/trials without an explicit spread statistic.

n_eval_types=5 approximates distinct evaluation angles (ROC/TP-FP classification performance, new-variant/generalization detection, computational complexity/runtime, adversarial mimicry-and-perturbation robustness, comparison to the PJScan baseline); boundaries between these categories are not sharply drawn by the paper itself.
